speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) - Crohn's Disease or Ulcerative Colitis. The patient's symptoms of chronic diarrhea, urgency, mucus, and relief of pain with defecation are classic for IBD. The history of a camping trip suggests a possible infectious trigger, but the chronicity (4 months) and specific symptoms point towards an inflammatory etiology. I will request a stool study to rule out infection and blood work to assess inflammation markers. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Culture, Stool_Ova_and_Parasites, Fecal_Calprotectin, CBC, ESR, CRP.
